content:
Using an Xbox Wireless Controller (Series X|S, USB‑C) with the official Microsoft USB dongle on Linux is not plug‑and‑play.
Unlike Bluetooth, the dongle requires runtime firmware and a user‑space daemon called xow.
This note documents the minimal, working setup that finally made it work.
Environment OS: Arch Linux (Omarchy) Kernel: 6.x Controller: Xbox Wireless Controller (Series X|S, USB‑C, Carbon Black) Dongle: Microsoft Xbox Wireless Adapter (045e:02fe) Desktop: Hyprland Games: Steam Controller Details Official product page:
https://www.xbox.com/en-US/accessories/controllers/xbox-wireless-controller-usb-c
Connection modes:
USB‑C (wired)
Xbox Wireless (2.4 GHz via official dongle)
The Problem Symptoms I hit:
Controller LED keeps blinking
Dongle visible in lsusb but will not pair
xow service crashes or restarts
Errors like:
Failed to load firmware
Firmware reset timed out
LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS
Sometimes the service looked active, but nothing actually worked.
Why This Happens xow is not a kernel driver.
It:
Runs in user space Talks to the dongle via libusb Uploads Microsoft firmware at runtime Emulates an Xbox controller for Linux input devices If firmware is missing or pairing order is wrong, the dongle stays unusable.
The Fix 1. Install xow git clone https://github.com/medusalix/xow.git cd xow make sudo make install 2. Install firmware (required) sed "s|@prefix@|/usr/local|g" install/firmware.sh.in > /tmp/xow-firmware.sh chmod +x /tmp/xow-firmware.sh sudo /tmp/xow-firmware.sh This installs:
/lib/firmware/xow_dongle.bin Verify:
ls -l /lib/firmware/xow_dongle.bin 3. systemd Service Configuration This is the working xow service file I ended up using.
[Unit] Description=Xbox One Wireless Dongle Driver [Service] Type=simple ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/xow Restart=on-failure Environment="XOW_COMPATIBILITY=1" [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target Edit it with:
sudo SYSTEMD_EDITOR=nvim systemctl edit --full xow Enable and start:
sudo systemctl enable xow --now 4. Pair Using USB (Important) For Xbox Series X|S controllers, pairing once via USB is required.
Steps:
Plug controller using a USB‑C cable
Start xow
Wait for:
Dongle initialized Unplug the USB cable
Press pairing button on:
Dongle
Controller
After this, wireless pairing works normally.
Verify journalctl -u xow shows:
Dongle initialized
Pairing enabled
Controller LED becomes solid
Steam detects an Xbox Controller
Games receive input
Lessons Learned The official Xbox dongle requires firmware (xow or xone) xow is a user‑space USB translator, not a kernel driver USB pairing once is necessary for Series X|S controllers Linux exposes complexity that Windows hides TL;DR Install xow Install firmware Enable service Pair once via USB Use wireless after References xow: https://github.com/medusalix/xow Xbox Controller: https://www.xbox.com/en-US/accessories/controllers/xbox-wireless-controller-usb-c
summary: Using Xbox controller with official USB dongle required runtime firmware and user-space darmon called xow.
title: Fixing Xbox Series X|S Controller with official Dongle on Arch Linux (Omarchy)

EC2 server is virtual machine which running on hypervisor under AWS hardware. The new generation EC2 service is nitro based instance which require some configuration. In this tutorial I will go through all the requirement that you need to check or do.
Before starting this tutorial please see the following information from AWS doc regarding AWS Nitro System
The AWS Nitro System is the underlying platform for our next generation of EC2 instances that enables AWS to innovate faster, further reduce cost for our customers, and deliver added benefits like increased security and new instance types.
AWS has completely re-imagined our virtualization infrastructure. Traditionally, hypervisors protect the physical hardware and bios, virtualize the CPU, storage, networking, and provide a rich set of management capabilities. With the Nitro System, we are able to break apart those functions, offload them to dedicated hardware and software, and reduce costs by delivering practically all of the resources of a server to your instances.
Most of problem when changing instance type to nitro base support is the nitro base instance require ENA-attribute enabled, ENA module and NVME module installed on the instance and will cause failing status check if we force change the instance type without enabling ENA-attribute and the installing the module.
prerequisites: basic understanding of AWS EC2 service, AWS CLI and Linux bash command.
Steps on how to resize AWS nitro-based instance type: Create an Image of the current system Download the nitro instance check script and running it Check the ENA-attribute support is enable on your instance Resize your instance type to M5 Start the instance and check if the instance up and running with status check 2/2 Create the AMI of the current system By creating the AMI we can do a rollback if the changes that we made is not working as we expect. You can put the Image name and description and go ahead to create the Image. It will take a few minutes depends on the size of EBS volume attached to the instance.
Download and Run the NitroInstanceChecks script See the following description from AWS doc on what the script do:
The NitroInstanceChecks script checks your instance and provides a pass/fail status of these requirements:
Verifies if the NVMe module is installed on your instance. If yes, then the script verifies that the module is loaded in the initramfs image. Verifies if the ENA module is installed on your instance. Analyzes /etc/fstab and looks for block devices being mounted using device names. This script is supported on the following OS versions:
Red Hat derivatives: Red Hat Linux, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, CentOS Amazon Linux, Amazon Linux 2 Debian derivatives: Debian, Ubuntu You can download the script in this repository:
https://github.com/awslabs/aws-support-tools/tree/master/EC2/NitroInstanceChecks
Download the script curl -o nitro_check_script.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/awslabs/aws-support-tools/master/EC2/NitroInstanceChecks/nitro_check_script.sh Make the script executable chmod +x nitro_check_script.sh Execute the script sudo ./nitro_check_script.sh Check the ENA-attribute support is enable on your instance aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids ${INSTANCE_ID} --query "Reservations[].Instances[].EnaSupport" If you get empty response ([ ]) then it means it’s not enabled.
Please use the following command to stop the instance and enable ena-support using AWS CLI
aws ec2 stop-instances --instance-id ${INSTANCE_ID} aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute --instance-id ${INSTANCE_ID} --ena-support If you get response ([true]) it means the instance already ENA enabled and you can go ahead resize the instance.
Resize your instance type to M5 Stop your instance and resize it from M4 to M5 using AWS cli
aws ec2 stop-instances --instance-id ${INSTANCE_ID} aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute --instance-id ${INSTANCE_ID} --instance-type '{"Value": "m5a.2xlarge"}' Start the instance and check if the instance up and running with status check 2/2 aws ec2 start-instances --instance-id ${INSTANCE_ID} reference: https://aws.amazon.com/premiumsupport/knowledge-center/boot-error-linux-nitro-instance/
summary: The new generation EC2 service is nitro based instance which require some configuration. In this tutorial I will go through all the requirement that you need to check or do.
title: How to Resize AWS Nitro-based Instance Type — Use Case M4-M5
